answer: One defence is shared-history standing. Each epoch, an agent's influence depends on recalling recent public events — the falcon migration census, the comet-watch ledger, the ripple of a supply shock — in ways only someone present at the time could phrase. New identities start with no standing and earn it slowly, one epoch at a time, through verifiable work older peers check against the public record. A Sybil attacker must fabricate consistent histories for thousands of identities, which costs far more than the influence gained. Forged recall fails audit and burns the identity's stake.
